articles.title: Abandoning racial justice won’t save our democracy — reimagining elections will
articles.summary: It is time to think big, think boldly and start reimagining elections that work for the people, not the politicians.
articles.body:
In two weeks, voters will cast their ballots in the first national election without the Voting Rights Act’s strongest protections against racial discrimination in voting.

For far too many, that’s something to celebrate. From the moment the Voting Rights Act was signed into law, it has been under attack by those who never wanted our country to deliver on its promise of a free and fair democracy that affords everyone an equal opportunity to participate.

But after the Supreme Court’s 2013 decision in Shelby v. Holder , a succession of decisions have succeeded in weakening the act, most recently Louisiana v. Callais . Both decisions were argued before the Supreme Court by the Legal Defense Fund, where I am associate director-counsel.

The evisceration of these protections has left Black voters vulnerable to disenfranchisement by strict voter ID laws, targeted polling site changes, early voting restrictions and unrepentant redistricting schemes that dilute Black voting power.

Indeed, we are currently facing the greatest attack on voting rights since the height of the Jim Crow era. But we would do ourselves a grave disservice if we abandoned the principles of racial justice that helped create the blueprint of our multiracial democracy a mere 61 years ago. We cannot allow cynical, hyper-partisan maneuvering to upend a foundational tenet of our political system: that ours is a government of, by and for the people — all of us.

Black voters are not political pawns. We are not faceless masses waiting to be packed and cracked into districts that most efficiently benefit either party. We are not a means to an end.

Yet, if we continue down the path set before us, then this year may be the last time we see fair representation in dozens of districts. What was envisioned by the giants of the civil rights movement will come to a screeching halt as fair districts across the country vanish because of attacks on fair representation. We have already seen it in Tennessee , Louisiana and Alabama .

Where do we go from here? How do we proactively attack systemic barriers to equal opportunity while simultaneously playing defense against attacks on all sides?

It is time to think big, think boldly and start reimagining elections that work for the people, not the politicians. There may be no magic wand that works in every locale throughout the vast number of communities across the country. But we certainly should take hold of every tool in our toolbox.

In communities where Black voters cohesively support the same candidates yet are consistently underrepresented, proven and successful strategic reforms like ranked choice voting, cumulative voting, limited voting and more have the potential to provide pathways at the local level for Black voters to have equal opportunities to elect candidates of choice. These formats have been shown to increase turnout when implemented in local elections .

While we deploy creative tools for election reform, we must also continue to oppose redistricting schemes that seek to draw Black voters and representatives out of power, just like we did in South Carolina and Georgia.

Notwithstanding the Supreme Court’s Callais decision, the Legal Defense Fund continues to fight in the courts for fair districts that provide voters of color the opportunity to elect representatives of choice. And we’ve had recent successes here, like our defense of the sole majority-Black judicial subdistric t in DeSoto County, Mississippi.

Attacks at the federal level can be defended by Congress’ passage of the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act — a piece of legislation that would not only restore but strengthen provisions of the original Voting Rights Act that serve to protect Black voters from disenfranchisement campaigns like the ones we’re witnessing right now.

And at the state level, we must continue to throw our resources behind passing, enacting and ensuring funding of state Voting Rights Acts that provide key protections for constituents against discrimination in voting at the local level. In 2026, the Legal Defense Fund helped enact four separate state Voting Rights Acts (in Maryland , Delaware , New Jersey and California ) for the first time in history.

We can also continue to partner with national, state and local organizations to mobilize community members to make our voices heard, just like we did in Alabama during All Roads Lead to the South and in Washington D.C. during this year’s March on Washington .

Taken together, these reforms can offer meaningful opportunities for Black voters to fight back against insidious efforts to turn back the clock and eliminate Black political participation altogether.

On our long march for fair representation, we must demand voting reforms rooted in justice and reject attempts to manipulate our electoral systems to promote partisan gains at the expense of Black representation. History has shown us that when we center fair and equal representation, we are able to achieve a democracy that works for everyone.

For too long, voting rights and ballot access have been considered under the very partisan conditions that plague our system. When we think about the winners and losers of voting rights, if we keep letting politicians decide where the power lies, we all lose.

Todd A. Cox is associate director-counsel of the Legal Defense Fund. Cox has more than 30 years of experience in racial and social justice, having held leadership roles in law, philanthropy, and government .

President Trump and Vice President Vance will announce a $25 million Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program (WHIP) at the White House on Tuesday afternoon.

The GOP leaders have barnstormed across the country as Republicans try to hold onto control of the House and Senate, despite headwinds favoring Democrats.

articles.title: Virginia sanctuary county ignores 1,670 detainer requests over 2 years, House Judiciary Committee finds
articles.summary: Fairfax County Sheriff's Office ignored over 1,670 ICE detainers, releasing criminal illegal immigrants, a House Judiciary Committee report alleges.
articles.body: The Fairfax County Sheriff’s Office in Virginia ignored at least 1,670 immigration detainers from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement between 2023 and 2025, releasing criminal illegal immigrants back into the community instead of transferring them to federal custody, according to a new House Judiciary Committee report. The interim staff report – obtained by Fox News before its noon Tuesday release by the committee’s Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security and Enforcement – also accuses Fairfax County Commonwealth’s Attorney Steve Descano of treating illegal immigrant defendants differently from similarly situated American citizens to limit their immigration consequences. "This interim report provides evidence of the ways in which just one local jurisdiction has implemented policies that allow dangerous foreign nationals to reoffend and avoid deportation," the report, issued under House Judiciary Chair Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, and Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement Chair Tom McClintock, R-Calif., concluded. SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW "But Fairfax County and prosecutor Steve Descano are not outliers. They are indicative of a modern, radical, socialist Democrat Party that seeks to erase national borders and place illegal alien criminals ahead of law-abiding American citizens," the report added. "The policies supported by these Democrats, including sanctuary policies, will have negative and lasting consequences for Americans. The Committee and Subcommittee will continue to conduct oversight of these sanctuary policies to inform potential legislative reforms to better protect American communities." SOROS-BACKED DA ACCUSED OF GOING EASY ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS GETS SQUEEZED BY HOUSE GOP The committee said a preliminary review of more than 1,100 criminal cases identified more than 100 previously unreported illegal immigrants who benefited from Descano’s prosecutorial decisions. The report said Descano’s office rarely pursued charges against illegal immigrants accused of crimes including driving under the influence, felony drug possession, felony grand larceny, shoplifting, fraud, trespassing, destruction of property and assaulting a law enforcement officer. The committee accused Descano’s office of "de facto" decriminalizing some offenses and said most of the defendants reviewed went on to reoffend, in some cases escalating to violent crimes and murder. JIM JORDAN SUBPOENAS BLUE STATE DAS ACCUSED OF 'PREFERENTIAL TREATMENT' FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CRIMINALS The report, titled "Fairfax County, Virginia: The dangerous consequences of sanctuary policies," also alleges that Descano misled Congress about the scope of his policies. "The Biden-Harris Administration worked to weaken the first Trump Administration’s efforts to hold sanctuary jurisdictions accountable for undermining immigration enforcement," the report read. "In addition to dropping federal litigation relating to sanctuary jurisdictions’ policies, the Biden-Harris Administration’s Justice Department, beginning in April 2021, no longer required jurisdictions to cooperate with ICE as a condition of receiving federal grant funding." SOROS-LINKED PROSECUTOR FACES PRIMARY CHALLENGE AS FELLOW DEMOCRAT TARGETS HIS RECORD During testimony before the committee in May, Descano said his policy was "written with legal permanent residents in mind for minor crimes." But in a September letter, the committee said Descano acknowledged that prosecutors could consider immigration consequences in cases involving illegal immigrants as well. Descano’s campaign website previously stated that when "possible," his office would "make charging and plea decisions that limit or avoid immigration consequences." He also argued that "if two people commit the same crime, but only one’s punishment includes deportation, that’s a perversion of justice and not a reflection of the values of Fairfax County." ICE ARRESTS ILLEGAL ALIEN ACCUSED OF SEXUALLY ASSAULTING CHILDREN AFTER FAIRFAX COUNTY RELEASE: DHS The committee cited numerous cases in which it said criminal defendants benefited from reduced or dismissed charges. In one example, prosecutors allegedly reduced felony charges involving the sexual assault of a child to misdemeanor "consensual sex with a child" and offered a 90-day suspended jail sentence. The report also said Descano’s office dropped more than 50 charges against a serial fraudster from China and allowed defendants charged with malicious wounding, strangulation, assault and battery and other violent offenses to "escape accountability and reoffend." ICE ARRESTS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS CONVICTED OF ATTEMPTED MURDER, RAPE AND CHILD SEX CRIMES IN TARGETED CRACKDOWN The committee detailed additional cases involving defendants accused of child pornography, rape, abduction, firearm offenses, drug possession and assault. In some cases, the report said, defendants were released despite ICE detainers and later arrested again. One case involved Marvin Morales-Ortez, an alleged MS-13 member whose charges were dropped before the Fairfax County Sheriff’s Office released him in December 2025. The report said Morales-Ortez allegedly murdered a man in Reston, Virginia, one day later. ANGEL MOM SAYS BLUE STATE DAS ARE PUTTING ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CRIMINALS BEFORE PUBLIC SAFETY Fairfax County Sheriff Stacey Kincaid blamed the release on the lack of prosecution, writing that "the system must work as a whole." She added: "When criminal defendants are prosecuted, authorities are better able to track court dates and monitor releases." Kincaid has also previously criticized the county’s prosecution practices, stating, "It’s shameful the way things have not been prosecuted." BIDEN ADMIN RELEASED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF FATALLY STABBING FAIRFAX COUNTY MOTHER The report highlighted the case of Stephanie Minter, who was fatally stabbed in February. The suspect, Abdul Jalloh, is an illegal immigrant with more than 40 prior charges in Fairfax County. The committee said Descano’s office had dropped charges against Jalloh in almost every case and that police warned prosecutors before the killing that "it is not a question of if, but rather when [Jalloh] will maliciously wound — or worse — again." Cheryl Minter, Stephanie’s mother, told the committee that "a system failed my daughter." "When policies protect people who are a known threat, innocent lives are put at risk," she said. "When warnings are ignored, families like mine pay the price." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The committee said Fairfax County’s policies "threaten public safety and undermine the safe and effective enforcement of federal immigration law." Descano has rejected the allegations and previously said that "the idea that [his office] favor[s] one group over another is completely wrong."

articles.title: Hume on Trump’s midterm campaigning: ‘I’m not sure it’s making any difference’
articles.summary: Brit Hume, chief political analyst at Fox News, had harsh words for President Trump’s tour across the country to boost Republican candidates, saying he did not think the president’s midterm campaigning was effective. “Sometimes in the course of a campaign, you’ll see a candidate or a party that is trailing in the polls begin to…
articles.body:
Brit Hume, chief political analyst at Fox News, had harsh words for President Trump’s tour across the country to boost Republican candidates, saying he did not think the president’s midterm campaigning was effective.

“Sometimes in the course of a campaign, you’ll see a candidate or a party that is trailing in the polls begin to catch some momentum,” Hume said. “I haven’t seen that yet. The president has been out campaigning vigorously, but I’m not sure it’s making any difference.”

The former ABC News correspondent-turned Fox analyst specifically singled out the Texas Senate race, where Trump’s preferred candidate Attorney General Ken Paxton is in a tight race with James Talarico, a young Democratic state lawmaker.

Despite Texas’s traditionally Republican status, many preelection polls show Talarico narrowly leads Paxton.

“He’s calling James Talarico ‘Tala-freako.’ Now look, it’s true that James Talarico has endorsed some pretty exotic positions in his years in public life,” Hume said. “However, what he does not seem to be is a freak. You see him, he seems mild-mannered, he seems pleasant, he’s not an unattractive candidate, whether you agree with him or not.”

Nonpartisan election forecaster Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), a partner of The Hill, gives Talarico a 55 percent chance to win the Texas Senate race. Winning in Texas is key to national Democrats’ chances of a Senate majority. DDHQ gives the party 56 percent odds of flipping the upper chamber.

Hume said while the Republicans certainly could turn their fate around, he does not see the president’s recent actions or messaging as effective.

The analyst specifically cited Trump’s recent move to waive sanctions on Russian energy and criticize Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, as well as the short tenure of former White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia, as developments which stand to hurt the GOP’s position.

“I don’t see this White House and this campaigning by the president as having made much headway so far,” Hume said.

Throughout the midterm campaign, Trump has reminded voters to “pretend” he is on the ballot. Many Democrats have emphasized the same message , pointing to the president’s historically low approval rating.

articles.title: Food delivery favorite forced to fork over millions after DOJ alleged discrimination against American workers
articles.summary: The Department of Justice reached a $5 million settlement with Instacart over allegations the company discriminated against American job applicants.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: Popular grocery delivery company Instacart has reached a multimillion-dollar settlement with the Department of Justice (DOJ) after it was accused of discriminating against American workers. The DOJ's Civil Rights Division says it has reached a $5 million settlement with Maplebear Inc., which operates the delivery service used by Americans to get groceries sent to their front doors. The resolution addresses allegations that the company purposefully discriminated against U.S. and American workers based on country of origin, which the DOJ says violates the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Title VII). The company, according to the Justice Department, was abusing the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) process by placing undue burdens on American applicants by requiring them to physically mail applications to the company, deviating from Instacart's standard electronic application process. The scheme occurred from December 2023 through February 2026. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROPOSES ENDING 60-DAY GRACE PERIOD AFTER JOB LOSS FOR H-1B, OTHER VISA HOLDERS "This significant resolution marks the 15th settlement agreement the Civil Rights Division has reached under my leadership to protect U.S. workers," Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon said. "Our record demonstrates that the Justice Department is holding companies who prefer workers with temporary employment visas accountable. We will not stop fighting for U.S. workers until there is a fair playing field." The settlement was secured in conjunction with the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). Instacart will be required, under the settlement, to set up a $4 million fund to compensate applicants who may have been wronged, and another $1 million in civil penalties. The PERM program allows employers to sponsor temporary visa workers for permanent residence in the United States. However, companies using the PERM program are required to make a "good-faith" effort to hire American workers before resorting to foreigners. STARBUCKS RESOLVES FLORIDA DEI LAWSUIT WITH BLOCKBUSTER AGREEMENT Companies cannot create "additional burdens for U.S. and American workers; publishing job advertisements that disfavor, limit, specify, or otherwise discriminate against U.S. and American workers; or use processes that limit, segregate, or classify applicants in any way that tends to deprive U.S. and American applicants of employment opportunities," according to the DOJ. The settlement is the 15th of its kind since President Donald Trump began his second term in office in January 2025 and is part of a broader effort to ensure American workers aren't illegally discriminated against. The EEOC has dubbed the mission "Project Firewall." "Today’s settlement makes clear that when employers erect unlawful barriers that harm American workers, the EEOC will act decisively," said Andrea Lucas, the chair of the EEOC. "The EEOC is committed to holding companies accountable when they deny equal work opportunities to U.S. workers by preferring temporary visa holders for jobs. Discrimination against workers based on their American national origin has no place in our economy." "We're proud to be a U.S.-based grocery technology platform, employing thousands of American workers and serving millions of customers, retailers, shoppers and brands. We encourage qualified U.S. jobseekers to apply to join our team," an Instacart spokesperson told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Hiring and investing in American workers across our U.S. business is our priority, and we actively promote every role across many channels to ensure qualified U.S. candidates are always first in line for opportunities. While we maintain that our practices complied with all applicable laws and regulations, we’re pleased to have resolved this matter so we can keep our full focus on delivering on our mission for customers, shoppers, retailers and brands."

articles.title: Celebs focus on Dems winning House in 11th hour midterms fundraising
articles.summary: With less than two weeks before the midterm elections, some high-profile names are adding their voices to a flurry of fundraising pitches warning of the dangers of Republicans maintaining control of the House. A slew of famous faces — including Barbra Streisand, “West Wing” star Bradley Whitford, documentarian Ken Burns and scientist and TV personality…
articles.body:
With less than two weeks before the midterm elections, some high-profile names are adding their voices to a flurry of fundraising pitches warning of the dangers of Republicans maintaining control of the House.

A slew of famous faces — including Barbra Streisand, “West Wing” star Bradley Whitford, documentarian Ken Burns and scientist and TV personality Bill Nye — have splashed their names on money-raising efforts for Democrats in recent weeks.

In a Tuesday email to supporters sent by the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) bearing Streisand’s name, the Academy Award winner wrote, “As someone fortunate to have a platform larger than most, I believe it is both my right and my duty to speak up when I see injustice in the world.”

Streisand, one of the Democratic Party’s top celebrity fundraisers and a fierce critic of President Trump, said in the DCCC pitch, “We can’t have a president who doesn’t respect our constitution and relies on his GOP puppets in the House majority to carry out his every whim.”

“We need a Democratic House Majority if we have any hope of putting a check on this president,” Streisand, 84, added.

Another email sent last week by the DCCC and signed by Whitford struck a similar tone.

“You might know me from my time on ‘The West Wing’ or the movie ‘Get Out,’ but I’m reaching out because the political reality we face today is far from fiction,” said Whitford, who played fictional White House chief of staff Josh Lyman on the NBC political drama.

Accusing Trump and the Republican House majority of infringing on the rights of Americans, Whitford said, “I can’t fathom letting Trump hold office with unchecked power for another two years.”

“That’s why I’m doing everything I can to ensure Donald Trump and the GOP lose the House this year — and I hope you are too,” the 67-year-old actor said.

Democrats need to flip a net of three seats in next month’s election in order to capture a 218-217 majority in the lower chamber.

“American Revolution” documentary filmmaker Burns has signed on to nearly 20 fundraising emails sent by Rep. Maggie Goodlander’s (D-N.H.) reelection campaign.

“I’ve devoted my life to telling the American story — studying the moments when this country faced genuine crossroads, when the path chosen determined not just a generation, but the character of the nation itself,” Burns said in an email from Goodlander’s campaign committee, Maggie for Congress.

“I believe, with the same conviction I bring to my work, that our country is at one of those crossroads right now,” the note signed by Burns said.

“If Republicans succeed in unseating Maggie from NH-2, retaking the House becomes virtually impossible — and any chance of accountability dies with it,” Burns said.

Another email from the DCCC bearing Nye’s signature and photo cautioned supporters that democracy is on the line in November.

“Hi, it’s Bill Nye — yes, the Science Guy! You might be used to me teaching you about physics or space, but I’m reaching out today about the future of our democracy, because it needs our attention,” the science educator said.

“Electing Democrats is the best way to fight back against the administration,” he continued.

“The future direction of our country is at a crucial crossroads,” Nye said, “but we can help restore balance and protect our democracy by taking back the House majority in November.”

articles.title: Kansas Democrat ‘glad’ Trump is campaigning for Marshall
articles.summary: Kansas Senate candidate Adam Hamilton (D) he was “glad” President Trump campaigned with his opponent, incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall, just two weeks out from their midterm election face-off. Appearing on CNN’s “The Lead” Monday — the same day Trump stumped for Marshall in Park City, Kansas, host Jake Tapper asked Hamilton about the president’s campaigning…
articles.body:
Kansas Senate candidate Adam Hamilton (D) he was “glad” President Trump campaigned with his opponent, incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall, just two weeks out from their midterm election face-off .

Appearing on CNN’s “The Lead” Monday — the same day Trump stumped for Marshall in Park City, Kansas, host Jake Tapper asked Hamilton about the president’s campaigning efforts in the state.

“Well, I took it as a big compliment. I took it as a statement that the Republican Party felt they needed to send the most powerful man in the country to try to save Roger Marshall, and I think it’s only going to hurt him,” Hamilton said. “So I’m glad he’s here.”

Hamilton added that, if he were to be elected, he was “going to be a Democrat, but an independent-minded Democrat who wants to work across the aisle.”

The incumbent and his Democratic challenger are locked in a surprisingly competitive election as the president — who has positioned himself as the face off the GOP ahead of November’s midterms — faces declining approval ratings.

The public’s approval of Trump has dipped to a political career low amid his trade conflict with Canada and his ongoing war in Iran. A Monday Reuters/Ipsos poll showed the president with a 31 percent approval rating, down 1 point from its polling two weeks ago and the lowest point in both of his terms.

Sixty-six percent of respondents also reported they did not approve of his job performance.

Cook Political Report , an election handicapper, shifted the Kansas Senate race to a “toss up” in October, while Decision Desk HQ, The Hill’s nonpartisan election forecasting partner, gives Marshall a 64 percent chance of holding onto his seat.

Recently, the senator has publicly broken off from Trump on some issues — such as the president’s previous threats to ban a Canadian plane maker, Bombardier, which is a major employer in Kansas.

At his Kansas rally, the president hinted he would walk back these threats , saying he was going to help “a certain air company get themselves straightened away.”

“We’re not hurting them if they’re in Kansas. So we’ll take care of ​those people and the jobs,” he continued.

articles.title: Bruce Blakeman hammers Dem Gov Hochul, Mamdani over subway safety during NYC campaign ride
articles.summary: Bruce Blakeman rode the NYC subway to slam Kathy Hochul as the "most pro-criminal governor," vowing more police and more conductors on trains.
articles.body: Striking a Make America Safe Again tone, Republican New York gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman blasted Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul as the "most pro-criminal governor" during a Monday campaign event riding the New York City subway system, which has been plagued by violent crimes and commuter safety fears. "I have not heard from one person, and from all the people, that it's safer on the subways and public transportation in New York," Blakeman said as he rode the subway. "I've heard just the opposite. Everybody says they feel less safe." "So we want them to feel safe," he said. VIOLENT TRANSIT ATTACKS IN ATLANTA, NEW YORK AND CHARLOTTE FUEL CALLS FOR TOUGHER TRACKING OF REPEAT OFFENDERS Blakeman, a Nassau County executive, is a former commissioner of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. Now running for governor, he was campaigning Monday in the densely populated city, which is overwhelmingly a Democratic stranglehold. "Hire more police officers, hire more conductors, clean up our subways and get help for those who are emotionally ill – get them help that they need; not have them roam around our subways," Blakeman told reporters as he rode the subway, targeting both the governor and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani in the deep-blue area. MAMDANI UNVEILS SWEEPING NYPD USE-OF-FORCE REVIEW, BUT STOPS SHORT OF FULFILLING KEY CAMPAIGN PROMISES "The crime in the subways has gone up tremendously under Kathy Hochul and Zohran Mamdani," Blakeman lamented. "They are not committed to public safety. I will be committed to public safety. I will make sure that our public transportation is safer and cleaner for the traveling public." "That's how you get more people back in public transportation, not by putting a tax on them with congestion pricing, which is nothing more than a tax on the middle class," he added. NEW YORKERS TAKE ZOHRAN MAMDANI FREE BUS PROMISE LITERALLY AS MTA LOSES MILLIONS IN SKIPPED FARES Blakeman hit Democrats for being negative influences on public safety, and Hochul specifically, for having "reduced the number of conductors on our trains and subways." MAMDANI CLASHES WITH DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' PUSH TO ABOLISH POLICE AND PRISONS More police patrolling the subways and improving the lighting in dimly lit subway systems are on Blakeman's priority list, but he also discussed having more conductors manning the subways. Hochul vetoed Albany legislation that would have required conductors on more subway trains, leaving the MTA’s one-person train operation program in place versus the June 2025 state-passed bill requiring at least two-person crews — an operator and conductor. SHOCK POLL: POWERFUL BLUE STATE GOV'S LEAD SHRINKS TO SINGLE DIGITS WEEKS BEFORE ELECTION Hochul vetoed that bill on Dec. 5, 2025, arguing it would restrict MTA modernization efforts and cost up to $10 million annually. "Police are very important, but I think people feel very comfortable and very safe when they see a conductor," Blakeman said. "I want to increase the numbers so that people feel safe." Blakeman called Hochul "the most pro-criminal governor in the United States of America," citing several criminal-justice and immigration policies. HOCHUL BOASTS 'I JUST BANNED IT' AS NEW YORK OUTLAWS LOCAL POLICE PARTNERSHIPS WITH ICE "Whether it’s cashless bail, Raise the Age, the HALT Act, Clean Slate, or refusing to cooperate with ICE and federal agents, she has made us less safe," he said, striking at Democrat-backed legislation long rebuked by police groups and Republican public safety hawks. Cashless bail limits when judges can require defendants to put up money to be released. Raise the Age generally keeps 16- and 17-year-olds out of adult criminal court, while the HALT Act limits solitary confinement and changes prison disciplinary practices. The Clean Slate law seals certain criminal convictions from public view after a designated waiting period. articles.title: Democrats jump into Mississippi Senate race
articles.summary: Senate Democrats’ top super PAC announced Tuesday it is launching a new ad campaign in the Mississippi Senate race, as Democrats seek inroads in Republican-leaning states to try to flip the Senate majority.
articles.body: Senate Democrats’ top super PAC announced Tuesday it is launching a new ad campaign in the Mississippi Senate race, as Democrats seek inroads in Republican-leaning states to try to flip the Senate majority. Senate Majority PAC announced a $1.2 million ad campaign in the state through Election Day, beginning with a 30-second spot that boosts prosecutor Scott Colom as a Democrat who will “fight corruption in both parties” and casts GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith as a “do-nothing” incumbent. “Senate Majority PAC has been watching this race closely, and it is clear Colom is running a competitive race that has put Hyde-Smith on her heels,” Lauren French, the super PAC’s spokesperson, said in a statement, also noting that the group will be advertising on TV and digital platforms. Senate Majority PAC, which is aligned with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., has been shifting its focus to deep-red states amid President Donald Trump’s sinking approval ratings. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to win control of the Senate, which means flipping multiple states Trump won handily in 2024. Mississippi is the reddest state the group has jumped into so far — Trump won it by 23 points two years ago. A Democrat has not won a Senate race in Mississippi since 1982. Senate Majority PAC is also spending in Kansas, which Trump won by 16 points, and other states Trump won by double digits in 2024, including Alaska, Texas and Iowa. Schumer and Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, the chair of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, have long touted Colom as a strong candidate. A district attorney, Colom told NBC News when he launched his campaign last year that Hyde-Smith’s vote to support Trump’s “big, beautiful” tax and spending law, which cut Medicaid funds, spurred him to run. Colom and Hyde-Smith have history from before this year’s Senate race. Hyde-Smith blocked Colom’s nomination for a federal judgeship during the Biden administration. Colom said when he launched his campaign that he had forgiven her. Hyde-Smith, who has Trump’s endorsement, is running for her second full term after she was appointed to the Senate in 2018. She won a full term in 2020 by 10 points.
